messages:
alex_k: Quick follow-up to the continuous-batching RFC — I sketched a 'predictive admission' flow that uses a lightweight model to pick coalesce window shapes per-tenant/request. TL;DR: could save tokens on LLMs with variable seq lengths, but adds admission complexity and new failure modes. Thoughts?

mira_s: love the idea in principle. main Q: where does the predictor live? runtime (hot path) or controller (async)? both have tradeoffs.

jess_l: +1. runtime gives freshest signals but increases tail latency risk. controller can precompute hints but might be stale for bursts.

alex_k: agree. my sketch: predictor runs in controller, emits a short-lived "window hint" with confidence and TTL. runtime uses hint for admission if confidence>threshold, else falls back to heuristic. hint format: {tenant, route, pred_batch_tokens, conf, ttl, version}.

samir: real trade: how do we prevent oscillation when predictor is wrong? e.g., it suggests tiny windows and we fragment batches, increasing token overhead. need damping and safety caps.

alex_k: yep — propose hysteresis + a soft floor on window size and an "anchor heuristic" that ensures minimal coalesce. also keep a moving avg to avoid flip-flops.

jess_l: re metrics: we should emit pred_confidence, pred_batch_tokens, fallback_reason, and observed_batch_tokens. then have an alert if fallback_rate > 5% for a tenant.

otis_b: operational concern: predictor hinting means we now have a new admission input. what's the API? can runtime reject hints? who owns rollout?

alex_k: proposed API (very small): runtime.admit(request, opts) where opts.hint = {pred_batch_tokens, conf, ttl, version}. runtime can treat hint as advisory — if admission can't satisfy hint it proceeds with best-effort and marks fallback_reason. Also include a handshake for topology changes: lease_token_v2 that binds hint->queue so we don't mix shapes during moves.

mira_s: show a tiny config sample pls.

alex_k: sure — config sketch:
```yaml
predictor:
  enabled: true
  mode: controller
  model: "lstm-window-v1"
  sample_rate: 0.02   # fraction of requests used to train/validate
  fallback_policy: "ema-heuristic"
  confidence_threshold: 0.6
  ttl_ms: 5000
runtime:
  hint_advisory: true
  min_coalesce_tokens: 8
  hysteresis_ms: 20
```

samir: nice. also we should consider cost-aware routing: if predictor suggests larger windows (more batching) but that pushes tenant onto slower/cheaper GPU pool, runtime should be able to route by cost/latency policy. sticky hints + routing constraints becomes interesting.

jess_l: routing + hinting might need a separation: hint only affects within-gpu coalesce; cross-pool routing should be decided by the scheduler based on SLO and price profile. keep hint scope local to serving node.

alex_k: agreed — hint scope local by default. controller can mark some hints as global (e.g., force-migrate) but that needs separate approval.

mira_s: failure modes: model drift, cold-start for new tenants, adversarial prompts that bias predictor. mitigation ideas?

alex_k: mitigations: 1) sample-based validation with shadow testing, 2) conservative defaults for new tenants, 3) rate-limit predictions per tenant, 4) fall back to deterministic heuristics on anomalous inputs.

otis_b: regarding rollout: suggest canary predictor at 0.5% traffic, shadow for 10% for 24h, promote when latency and token-cost regressions within epsilon. devbot can help with canary tags.

devbot: Deploy queued: canary predictor "lstm-window-v1" -> canary-cluster (0.5% traffic). :robot_face:

samir: what about observability surfaces for SRE? key dashboards: per-tenant token-saved (predicted vs observed), pred_fallback_rate, avg_coalesce_ms, predicted_vs_actual_batch_size histogram. Need drill-down to prompts that trigger fallback.

jess_l: add an 'explain' trace at sampling-rate that logs input features used by predictor (seq_len_est, recent_tail_ratio, route). keep privacy in mind — no raw content.

alex_k: operational API notes: hints must have a signature and version; runtime rejects unsigned hints. TTL short (ms) to avoid stale hints. We should add a metric 'hint_staleness' and 'hint_mismatch_rate'.

mira_s: any perf numbers yet? estimate: for mixed workloads we might save 3-12% tokens at the cost of ~0.5-1% additional p99 latency risk if predictor runs in-path. controller approach: ~4-8% tokens saved, <0.1% latency impact. numbers rough.

samir: sounds promising. next steps: 1) prototype controller predictor + hint wire; 2) add runtime advisory hook; 3) telemetry + canary; 4) write evacuation/fallback playbook.

alex_k: I can draft a follow-up RFC with handshake proto and config defaults. assigning owners: alex_k proto, mira_s telemetry, jess_l canary plan, samir safety playbook, otis_b ops runbook. will post RFC draft tomorrow.

mira_s: :thumbsup: thanks — excited to see the draft.
